evidence: Liv. 37.46.10: sex mīlia familiārum cōnscrīberet (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: To write together in a list: the standing word for enlisting troops, and for enrolling colonists or a class of citizens; hence patrēs cōnscrīptī. To hire staff is condūcere (see employ).

terms.grammar: verb phrase: dēlēctus (dīlēctus), dēlēctūs m.; habeō, habēre
evidence: Caes. BG 6.1: per lēgātōs dēlēctum habēre (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 186: draft, dīlēctus; to hold a draft, dīlēctum habēre
terms.comment: “A standing phrase for recruiting” (Lewis & Short); dēlēctum agere is post-Augustan. dēlēctus is the choosing and the levy itself (see choice).

terms.gloss: a recruit, a new soldier; a beginner
terms.comment: Also a beginner at anything: in forō tīrō, new to the courts (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: take in, admit (as a member, a citizen, an ally)
evidence: Cic. Arch. 4: nōn modo nōn sēgregandum ā numerō cīvium vērum etiam adscīscendum (Lewis & Short, s.v. sēgregō)
terms.comment: For recruiting someone into a group by choice; see also adopt.

terms.gloss: give in one’s name, enlist (of the recruit)
evidence: Lewis & Short s.v. nōmen: “to give in one’s name, be enrolled, enlist”
Liv. 2.24: nē nōmina darent (Lewis & Short s.v. nōmen)
